script: Spread and total were not saved, so this PHI@CHI script is form-only from weeks 1-2. PHI has split 52 listed rushes among Saquon Barkley (19/92), Tank Bigsby (14/36), Jalen Hurts (10/64) and Will Shipley (9/28), while CHI has piled 70 listed rushes on D'Andre Swift (34/169), Kyle Monangai (20/147) and Caleb Williams (15/107). Chicago blitzes 39% and Hurts' EPA/dropback drops from 0.20 with no blitz to 0.12 vs blitz (n=22), so PHI's path is Barkley/Hurts runs and shorter targets, not a 267-air-yard Devonta Smith script. PHI blitzes only 22%, so Williams spends most dropbacks in the no-blitz look where his EPA is 0.27 (n=45) versus 0.23 vs blitz, a cleaner pocket for Swift's 6 targets/64 yards and the Kalif Raymond (14/124) and Luther Burden (12/95) target stack.
who_goes_off: Devonta Smith is the PHI pass-game piece most built for Chicago's leak: 19 targets, 170 yards and 267 air yards in two games, into a CHI defense allowing 10.5 YPA on 14 middle attempts and 9.65 YPA on 17 right-side attempts with 7 passes of 20+ on 63 attempts. On the CHI side Kyle Monangai is the explosive, not just the complement to Swift's 34 carries: 147 yards on 20 carries (7.35 YPC) plus 35 receiving yards on 4 targets, against a PHI run defense that has already allowed 7 runs of 10+ despite a 4.16 YPC average.
weak_spot: Chicago's real leak is the middle of the field at 10.5 YPA on 14 attempts, with the right side also soft at 9.65 YPA on 17 attempts versus 7.15 YPA on 27 left-side attempts, and the run front has allowed 4.88 YPC plus 5 runs of 10+. Philadelphia's map is the opposite: left side is the soft pass zone at 7.85 YPA on 13 attempts, the middle is their best area at 5.17 YPA on 12 attempts, the right is 6.31 YPA on 29 attempts, and they have still allowed 7 runs of 10+ at 4.16 YPC.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for PHI@CHI, so there is no fallout to reprice: Barkley's 19-carry share, Swift's 34-carry lead, and the tight-end split of Dallas Goedert (7 targets/81 yards), Cole Kmet (4/35) and Colston Loveland (5/3) have to be treated as the current roles.
qb_vs_blitz: Jalen Hurts is the blitz downgrade at 0.12 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=22) against 0.20 with no blitz, and Chicago's 39% blitz rate should push PHI toward Barkley's 4.84 YPC and Hurts' own 6.4 YPC on 10 carries rather than Smith's 267 air yards. Caleb Williams is playable against pressure at 0.23 EPA vs blitz (n=45) and slightly better without it at 0.27, and PHI's 22% blitz rate leaves most of his dropbacks in that better no-blitz bucket.

picks.why: Monangai has 147 rush yards and 35 receiving yards on 20 carries and 4 targets across weeks 1-2, a 91.0 rush+rec per-game rate against a 52.5 line at -116.5. Even if his 7.35 YPC regresses all the way to PHI's 4.16 YPC allowed on a 10-carry share (41.6 rush yards) and he keeps only his 17.5 receiving yards per game, that is 59.1, and PHI has already allowed 7 runs of 10+ so the chunk-run profile that produced 147 yards on 20 carries still has a path through this front.

Loveland has 3 receiving yards on 5 targets and 43 air yards in two games, 1.5 yards per game, against an under 32.5 at -114. PHI's middle, the tight-end zone, is their best coverage area at 5.17 YPA on 12 attempts, PHI blitzes only 22% so Williams is not forced off his better 0.27 no-blitz EPA into quick TE dumps, and Cole Kmet has taken 4 targets for 35 yards in the same window.
